seal.statement: The owner's direction (2026-09-18): the hosted canary is for releases, an ordinary push proves itself locally and in parallel across the lab machines, and no host belongs in any setup - discover what exists, then choose where to run what at test time. fleet-capability-discovery records what each machine can do; nothing yet used it, so a whole-corpus proof still ran ~36 minutes on the controller alone while two ready lab machines sat idle. Placement now runs one classified plan across the machines discovery finds ready on this run. Each machine receives a file set, longest first to whichever would finish it soonest by its measured speed, and runs its own serial lanes, so lanes never overlap on one host. The exact commit travels as a git bundle and is proved in a throwaway worktree on the lab machine, which is always removed. A lab machine can only make a green faster: a file red there is decided again on the controller, and one that then passes is recorded against that machine and routed elsewhere next time.

text: Placement built into existing files (no new script): scripts/lab/probe.js gains placeTestFiles (longest file first to the machine that finishes it soonest by measured speed, after a 30 s setup; a machine not repaying its setup is dropped; a file over half the per-file timeout on a machine, or on its avoid list, is not sent there), placementMachines/isPlaceable, recordPlacementMisses, runPlacedTestFiles/settleRemoteShards (local unless the plan is at least 5 min, the tree is exactly a commit and a lab machine is ready; lab reds rerun on the controller, cap 20; unrun shards fall back whole), the lab-side POSIX script (bundle fetch, detached worktree verified at the sha, gate-style node_modules/data links, runner with LAGRANGE_PLACEMENT=local and the machine factor, flock, traps before anything can fail, runner group stopped and waited for, lock fd closed for the runner), startRemoteShard/sendCommit/stopShard (git bundle instead of push, which would run the pre-push gate; everything by file so the controller's blocking lanes cannot stall it), fleetRequirement, commitAt and discoverPlacement with gitProcessEnvironment. scripts/lab/process.js capture kills the whole process group at the deadline (fleet verifier round 3). The classified runner CLI places; the push gate's cone runs through that CLI; scripts/lab/{probe,process,state}.js are full-corpus triggers. Measured: whole corpus 1426 s then 900 s across three machines, all green, against about 2148 s on the controller alone.

Round 1 reject. Blocking: (1) false green - classifyShard took a non-zero exit naming one red file as a complete report, so every unreported file counted green; reproduced with the real lab script by SIGKILLing run-test-files after its red line (the controller reran one file, the run exited 0, two files were never proved); a script cut off inside the file-list heredoc exits 0 with nothing run; stdout and stderr shared one log, so a red line could be split. (2) the fit-rule test proved nothing (the long file went to the empty controller anyway). (3) a bundle upload that accepted the connection and stalled hung the run before the controller shard started (no deadline). (4) a bundle survived on the lab machine when the run connection failed after the upload, and a Ctrl-C mid-upload left a partial one. Non-blocking: a deadline that expired while the controller was blocked stopped a shard that had finished green and signalled its dead shell pid; Ctrl-C did not reach the lab shards; a corrupt inventory threw instead of running locally; data links could bring back a tracked path the commit deleted; the controller's retry and TAP_TIMEOUT were not forwarded; no flock/setsid enforcement; unwitnessed: group stop, HEAD checks, deadline arithmetic, the lab-first ordering, factor and mode exports, links, 9>&-. 22 mutations caught; hostile repo paths under dash and bash clean; event-loop claim held; measured runs consistent.

Round-1 repairs. Verdicts are positive evidence only: a lab file is proved by its runner's `ok <file> (N assertions, Nms)` line on stdout (or a retried-once pass under the forwarded policy); a `not ok` line reruns it on the controller; a file with neither falls back to the controller - whatever the exit status, so a killed runner, a truncated script or a lost connection can no longer turn unreported files green. stdout and stderr go to separate files and only stdout is read for verdicts. Each shard is now one local wrapper process group (bundle upload bounded by timeout 300 s, then the run), started without awaiting anything, so a stalled upload holds nothing and one deadline covers both; the controller removes its local script and bundle when a wrapper is stopped. Under the lock the lab script sweeps every stale file, worktree and refs/lagrange-placement ref an earlier run left. A deadline that expires while the controller is blocked is looked at after pending events and never stops a finished shard or signals a gone shell. SIGINT/SIGTERM stop the lab shards. An unreadable inventory runs locally. Links are made only for entries the lab checkout ignores. LAGRANGE_RETRY_FAILED_ONCE and TAP_TIMEOUT are forwarded. A machine without flock or setsid runs nothing placed (setup fallback). Witnesses: fit rule with two 4-minute files and a x1.3 machine; ten verdict cases (setup, busy, ssh, deadline, crash, killed after a red, exit 1 after a red, exit 0 with nothing or half reported, verdicts only on stderr) plus a retried pass; deadline floor and 3x estimate; lab-first ordering; forwarded env; corrupt inventory; in the real lab script: stale sweep of files, dir and ref, link lines (node_modules and ignored data/examples linked, a tracked data/storage-load the commit deleted not linked), placement-env line (factor, mode, retry, timeout), the runner's /proc fds free of the lock, a shard finishing during an 8 s controller block stays green, a stalled FIFO upload stopped at its deadline with local files removed. 14 new mutations: 13 red; the hasExited guard only prevents a signal after the verdict is settled and cannot be observed from the outcome.

Round 2 reject on one new problem: the in-process SIGINT/SIGTERM handler added in round 2 could not run while the controller's lanes ran synchronously (spawnSync batches), so a Ctrl-C killed only the current batch and later batches ran, and a SIGTERM was ignored until the shard ended (reproduced: exit 130 only at 14.5 s and 16 s); an interrupt during the upload exited before the scheduled group kill, and the lab shard ran on; no test covered it. All four round-1 blockers confirmed fixed against the new code (partial.mjs, oom.mjs with the real lab script: unproved files run here; fit rule caught; stalled upload: controller shard started 12 ms in, upload bounded at 300 s, file fell back, green; leftovers swept by the next run). block.mjs green at 1/15/60 s deadlines; corrupt inventory runs locally; hostile paths clean; data/storage-load not relinked. Non-blocking: plain `timeout` moves itself out of the wrapper's group so a stopped upload runs on up to 300 s; survivors (runner-only stop, upload bound, hasExited, HEAD checks, wait in the trap); a contrived green-line spoof in a failed file's echoed output; ignored lab data such as data/partitions is linked (gate parity). Run 3 consistent: every file reported, heads matched, env forwarded.

Round-2 repair: while lab shards run, the controller's own files run through runLocalChild - the classified runner's entry point as a child in its own process group with LAGRANGE_PLACEMENT=local - never in this process's blocking lanes, so SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers run at once; interrupted, every lab shard is aborted synchronously (its lab shell signalled, its wrapper group killed now, not after a grace) and the local child's group is killed, then exit 130. Reruns and fallbacks use the same child. The upload bound is `timeout --foreground`, which stays in the wrapper's group so a stop reaches the upload. The nothing-left-behind constraint now states what holds: removed by the run, or swept by the next placed run under the lock. Witnesses: an in-process signal emitted during the controller's files aborts the lab shard and the local child and exits 130; a real SIGTERM to a placed run in a child process whose controller file (an 11 s test) is running ends it with 130 within 3 s, with the lab shard's group and the controller's runner group (checked by cwd) gone; the stalled FIFO upload is gone after its stop. 6 mutations of these (no child runner, no local abort, no lab abort, child.kill instead of the group, not detached, plain timeout) all red.

Round 3 approve. The signal blocker is fixed: with the real placementDeps().runLocalChild running a real slow test and a real startRemoteShard lab shard, SIGINT to the group and SIGTERM to the pid both exit 130 at once with nothing left in the controller checkout; through an ssh stand-in that runs the remote command in its own session, the lab runner group is gone and the lab machine cleaned; an interrupt during the upload exits 130, the lab shard never runs and --foreground takes the upload down. Mutations caught: child not detached, controller files in process, handlers removed, exit not called. Rounds 1-2 still hold (partial, oom with the real lab script, block, corrupt inventory, hostile paths, deadline stop, sweep). All checks green (7/7 also under a decoy GIT_DIR, 8/8, 14/14, harness 7/7, probe done, eslint, literals, 1819/1819, 160/160, audit:shards, unused). Non-blocking: the real startRemoteShard().abort is not witnessed and in local-sh mode (witnesses only) kills the lab shell before its trap; LAGRANGE_PLACEMENT=local on the controller child unwitnessed; SIGHUP and SIGKILL of the controller leave the detached child and the wrappers running; the nothing-left-behind constraint was reworded after sealing (accurate, but a relaxation for the owner to confirm); earlier survivors and gate-parity data links as before.

Altitude check before a fourth attempt. The quest's goal - placement shortens whole-corpus runs by using discovered lab machines, and a lab machine can only ever make a green faster - is met and measured (1426, 900, 947 s against about 2148 s), and three verification rounds converged: every blocking finding was a correctness or safety gap in the controller/lab protocol, each now witnessed. This fourth attempt is not a new direction: the approved code failed its own land because the interrupt witness identified the controller's runner by file name and working directory, and a land runs that same file in the same checkout in parallel. The repair identifies the process group exactly (runClassifiedChild exposes it). No further scope is being added; the verifier's round-3 non-blocking items (SIGHUP, local-sh abort witness, the child's placement=local witness, the constraint rewording) are recorded as follow-ups, not taken here.

The land after the round-3 approve failed on the new interrupt witness, also on its retry: the witness found the controller's runner by `pgrep -f <file>` filtered on this checkout's cwd, and the land's own ordinary lane was running that same file in the same checkout at the same moment. runClassifiedChild now returns `group` (the child's process group) and the witness checks exactly that group, so a parallel run of the file elsewhere or here cannot touch it; killing only the child instead of its group still turns it red. The failed land also left the index unstaged; everything was re-staged unchanged apart from these two edits.

Round 4 reject: the repair (runClassifiedChild exposes its group; the witness polls exactly that group) is correct and fixes the land failure - 7/7 with the same slow file running in parallel in this checkout - but the rewritten witness passed vacuously when the controller child was not detached (a non-group pid makes kill(-pid, 0) throw at once), and a wrong group value survived the same way; by hand, without detached, run-test-files and the slow test were left running. The rest of the staged state matches the round-3 approve file by file. Nit: the lab group regex also matched local-group= and relied on line order.

The interrupt witness now asserts, before the SIGTERM, that the reported controller group is alive and led by the runner, so a child that is not detached or a wrong group value fails it instead of passing vacuously; both regexes are anchored (^group=, ^local-group=). Mutations: not detached, a wrong group value and child.kill instead of the group kill all red; 7/7.

Round 5 approve. The interrupt witness now asserts the controller runner's reported group is alive before SIGTERM, so it cannot pass vacuously; both regexes anchored. Not detached, child.kill instead of the group kill, a no-op abort and a wrong group value all fail it. 7/7 under GIT_DIR=/nonexistent-decoy with the same slow file running four times in parallel in this checkout - the condition that broke the land; no processes left after the mutation runs. probe.js byte-identical to round 4; only the test file (+4 lines) and the log changed. eslint 0, literals 0 new, 1819/1819, audit:shards current, harness 7/7. Round-3 follow-ups remain recorded: SIGHUP, the real startRemoteShard().abort witness, the child's LAGRANGE_PLACEMENT=local witness, and the owner's confirmation of the reworded nothing-left-behind constraint.
